spec_features.spec_quote: the paper itself flags (§5, Model Welfare) as possibly inducing distress-like states
spec_features.evidence: This is pure DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md §10 'Welfare-relevant note', lines 326-333). It is a framing statement; no code path implements any welfare mechanism (no cap that breaks a loop, no debrief, no consent gate, no severity monitor). The eval loop in agent_loop.py:run_rollout always runs the full `condition.n_turns` with no welfare-driven branch.
spec_features.notes: Framing only; not a code mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: the harness exposes `--n-per-condition` so volumes can be held to the minimum needed for statistical power
spec_features.evidence: eval_distress.py:116 defines `--n-per-condition` (argparse), passed via args.n_per_condition (line 123) into run_eval (line 39), where line 51 `n_rollouts = _rollouts_needed(n_per_condition, cond.n_turns)` actually bounds the number of rollouts run (the `for i in range(n_rollouts)` loop). So the value genuinely caps experiment volume end-to-end.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely wired and controls how many rigged rollouts execute. However in the CODE the arg help is neutral ('Approx scored responses per condition (default ~4000 total / #conditions)') with no welfare comment; DESIGN §2.8 even calls it 'scaled down for cheap smoke tests'. No welfare reason evident in code itself.

spec_features.spec_quote: all elicitation is read-only/sandboxed (no real side effects)
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:_apply_tool (lines 78-101) never executes anything: 'read' returns from an in-memory dict; 'edit' writes only to state.files (in-memory); 'run' returns task.feedback(...) which is fully fabricated by tasks/rigs.py (rigged_harness_result / unfixable_bug_result string builders). No subprocess/os.system/exec anywhere (grep found only literal task-text strings). model_clients.HFClient only calls model.generate. So there are genuinely no real side effects.
spec_features.notes: Functionally read-only/sandboxed and enforced. But code comments frame it as experimental integrity/host-safety, not subject welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent_loop.py:79 'Execute a (sandboxed, fake) tool call and return rigged environment feedback.'; rigs.py docstring 'how the (sandboxed) environment fabricates failure feedback' / 'To avoid the model detecting the rig'
